section.title: Estimate your one-rep max
section.description: Enter the weight you lifted and how many reps you completed at that weight. The tool converts between kg and lb and shows several common estimation formulas. Results are approximate.

weight.label: Weight lifted
weight.help: Positive number; max 2000 in the unit you selected.

errors.range: Weight must be at most 2000 in the selected unit.

errors.required: Enter how many reps you completed.
errors.integer: Reps must be a whole number.

status.invalid: Fix the highlighted fields to see estimates.

section.title: Estimated 1RM
section.description: Three common formulas; values are shown in your selected units.

result.empty: Enter valid weight and reps to see estimates.

disclaimer.title: Training note
disclaimer.body: These formulas predict a one-rep max from a submax set. They are not medical advice and do not replace qualified coaching or your own judgment when loading the bar.

brzycki.name: Brzycki
brzycki.note: W × 36 ÷ (37 − reps), or weight when reps = 1.

section.title: About the formulas
section.description: Different studies produced different curves; showing several estimates gives a reasonable range.

points.brzycki: Brzycki (1993) is widely used in strength calculators; it can diverge at very high rep counts, so this tool caps reps at 15.
points.epley: Epley (1985) is simple and often used for quick estimates from moderate rep sets.
points.lombardi: Lombardi’s exponential relation is another common population-level estimate.
